text:
ashley: heads up - since ~0400 we've seen a spike in model fetch failures during node boot in eu-west edge clusters. GPU nodes are failing init because they can't resolve internal image registry, causing the autoscaler to repeatedly provision and then delete GPUs.

raj: seen it. logs show `lookup registry.internal.redwood: no such host` from kubelet. It looks DNS-related, not auth.

marcos: any correlation with the egress NAT changes we rolled yesterday? we flipped the nat gateway to the new pool for cost reasons.

ashley: yes suspected. dig from a problematic node:
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> registry.internal.redwood @10.0.0.2
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 12345
;; flags: qr aa rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 1
;; SERVER: 10.0.0.2#53(10.0.0.2)
;; WHEN: Wed Mar 17 04:17:02 UTC 2026
;; MSG SIZE  rcvd: 81
```

ashley: and /etc/resolv.conf shows: `nameserver 10.0.0.2
search redwood.local svc.cluster.local
options ndots:5`

kate: ndots:5 is our default in kubelet. But split-horizon resolver on 10.0.0.2 should answer internal names. If the NAT pool changed, maybe the upstream sees queries from an unexpected IP and returns NXDOMAIN or rate-limits.

marcos: i pulled network traces - lots of TCP retries to 10.0.0.2:53 and intermittent UDP ICMP unreachable. conntrack on the NAT boxes shows high ephemeral port reuse. could be port exhaustion + NAT fold causing truncated queries.

raj: i've also seen `server misbehaving` in CoreDNS logs around the same time window. Might be the resolver healthcheck failing under load and returning SERVFAIL.

ashley: this is hitting GPU provisioning path because the node init does `docker pull registry.internal.redwood:5000/model:vX`. When DNS fails, kubelet marks container as failed and autoscaler tears down the node, then tries again -> thrash and spikes cost.

cloudinfra-bot: alert: dns_query_error_rate eu-west-edge > 4x baseline for service=registry.internal.redwood (04:12-04:30 UTC) :eyes:

marcos: short remediation ideas: 1) temporarily point /etc/resolv.conf on new nodes to a known-good resolver (10.0.0.10) via kubelet extraConfig 2) reduce ndots to 2 for the bootstrap path 3) add a DNS caching sidecar on the host to reduce upstream load.

kate: can we just pin image pulls to use the public edge egress path (bypass split-horizon) as a short term workaround? It'll increase cost but stop thrash.

raj: we tested forcing egress via the public NAT for image pulls with `iptables -t nat -A OUTPUT` on a staging VM and image pulls succeeded consistently. But that won't solve internal service discovery failures for app traffic.

ashley: proposed immediate steps: 1) pause autoscaler rollouts for the next 30m 2) change bootstrap resolv to 10.0.0.10 for new nodes 3) revert last NAT gateway pool change if we see no improvement. I'll open a rollback PR if needed. :arrow_double_up:

marcos: i'll add temporary hostCache (dnsmasq) to the node init script and push an image with ndots:2 modification to the bootstrap kubelet config.

cloudinfra-bot: action_required: create incident INC-2026-034 for cross-team investigation (dns + nat + autoscaler)

kate: tagging security and platform ops. @sec-team @platform-ops - could NAT IP changes affect access control for the registry? we might need to whitelist the new pool.

ashley: good call. registry ACL logs show several DENY entries for the new nat pool IP range starting at 04:10 UTC. That's likely contributing to lookup failures when registry returns authoritative NXDOMAIN for unknown client or is configured to rate-limit.

raj: tracking notes: - verify conntrack counters on nat box - check firewall ACLs on registry - instrument coredns upstream latency and error codes - verify host resolv config during bootstrap

marcos: i'll take nat/conntrack, raj take CoreDNS and coredns plugins, kate take registry ACLs, ashley will coordinate autoscaler and node bootstrap changes.

ashley: thanks all. i'll post updates here. short term: manual pin to 10.0.0.10 for new nodes and pause autoscaler. medium term: dns-cache + review NAT pool + registry ACL whitelist.

kate: update: applied pin to 10.0.0.10 in staging bootstrap, new node came up and pulled images fine. rolling to eu-west now. :white_check_mark:

ashley: eu-west rolling now. will monitor dns_query_error_rate and autoscaler events.

cloudinfra-bot: update: dns_query_error_rate back to 1.1x baseline (04:42 UTC). incident INC-2026-034 created.

raj: follow-up: need to change prometheus alert to split SERVFAIL vs NXDOMAIN and add ndots-sensitive dashboards for bootstrap path. NXDOMAIN spikes look different than SERVFAIL for this incident.

marcos: opened PR for boot script dnsmasq and ndots tweak: link: https://git.redwood.internal/infra/boot-config/pulls/112

ashley: closing loop - after whitelist + pin + dnsmasq we saw stable node provisioning and GPU pool stabilized. leaving incident open for postmortem. :pray:
